alternatives.root_cause: Payment's process froze while its socket kept accepting, so callers saw no spans from it.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process writes nothing, but payment's log keeps emitting completed-transaction entries through 18:42 (tr_2e9893f112c9), and checkout's Charge spans return in milliseconds rather than hanging to a deadline (tr_82e98fc958fd).

alternatives.root_cause: Payment was cut off from the network and could not reach its dependencies or the collector.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned service logs that it cannot reach anything; payment's log instead shows successful transactions, and checkout's calls into payment still complete normally (tr_82e98fc958fd).

alternatives.root_cause: A bad artifact was rolled out to payment and the running version is wrong.
alternatives.why_not: The only change in the 24h window is an environment variable update, not an image or version change (tr_89dc29f170c1), and the running service still reports its expected version and serves charges.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout became slow waiting on payment, degrading the order path.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout and frontend error ratios are statistically unchanged from baseline (tr_78a31f293de1, tr_84ed1e61272d) and Charge spans are a few milliseconds, so nothing waited.

verdict.summary: A config change set payment's OTLP traces endpoint to a loopback address that has no collector listening, so payment stopped exporting spans and its telemetry vanished while the service itself kept serving charges normally.
verdict.reasoning: The payment error-ratio query returned no samples at all for the incident window (tr_4124a92d33e8) - an absence of spans, not a rise in error spans, which is what triggered the alert. Payment's own log is alive and writing normal completed-transaction records right up to the end of the window (tr_2e9893f112c9), so it is neither frozen nor silent nor complaining of unreachability. Checkout traces before 18:34 contain payment child spans under the Charge call, while traces at 18:34:59 and 18:35:29 show the Charge span with no payment child and no error (tr_82e98fc958fd) - the call still succeeds in a few milliseconds, only the callee's span is missing. The change log for payment holds exactly one change, at 18:34:18, pointing the OTLP traces endpoint at a loopback address (tr_89dc29f170c1), which lines up with the moment payment's spans stop appearing. Downstream checkout and frontend error ratios are flat against baseline (tr_78a31f293de1, tr_84ed1e61272d), confirming no user-visible failure propagated. The failing mechanism is a configuration value that names the wrong destination; the wrongness of that address is the fault.
open_questions: Why the declared onset is 18:41:16 when the config change landed at 18:34:18 and spans stopped around then - the gap is unexplained by what I looked at.
Whether the loopback endpoint is genuinely wrong for this deployment or whether a sidecar collector was expected to be present and is itself absent or dead.
Whether anything other than telemetry was affected; I did not inspect payment's own non-trace metrics (CPU, memory, charge throughput) to rule out a concurrent real degradation.
Whether a similar endpoint change was applied to other services by the same automation actor.
